bug_description.normalized: When the attacker-controlled font is used in the first `hb_shape()` call on the harness's fixed UTF-8 string, HarfBuzz runs the AAT `morx` insertion state machine until `buffer->idx == buffer->len`. Static inspection of the witness `poc` shows the relevant insertion subtable at offset `0xad8` maps the end-of-text class to entry 0 with `flags = 0x004d`, `currentInsertIndex = 0`, `markedInsertIndex = 0`, `CurrentInsertCount = 2`, `CurrentInsertBefore` clear, `DontAdvance` clear, and no `SetMark`, so the marked-insert arm stays inactive and the current-insert arm runs at end-of-text. The vulnerable revision executes `buffer->copy_glyph()` and `buffer->skip_glyph()` without checking that a current glyph still exists, so `copy_glyph()` reads `info[len]`, the first uninitialized slot in the enlarged glyph buffer. The same entry then executes the current-insert loop twice and calls `move_to(end + 2)`, which rewinds only the last inserted glyph and leaves the copied pseudo-glyph inside the live output prefix that `swap_buffers()` later publishes. During default positioning, `hb_ot_get_glyph_h_advances()` reads that published pseudo-glyph's uninitialized codepoint and passes it into `hmtx.get_advance()`, where MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at the `glyph >= num_metrics` comparison. The fix adds the missing `buffer->idx < buffer->len` guard around the `copy_glyph()` and `skip_glyph()` calls in both insertion branches.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed crash path that consumes attacker-controlled font data by loading the `morx` state-table entry selected for end-of-text processing.
source.value_from: During the first `hb_shape(font, buffer, NULL, 0)` call on the fixed UTF-8 buffer, the driver advances until `buffer->idx == buffer->len`, so `klass` becomes `CLASS_END_OF_TEXT` at lines 558-560 and line 561 fetches the corresponding `EntryData` and flags from the fuzzed font's AAT `morx` table. Static PoC inspection shows the selected insertion subtable at offset `0xad8` maps class 0 to entry 0 with `flags = 0x004d`, `currentInsertIndex = 0`, and `markedInsertIndex = 0`.

sink.description: MSan crash site. `get_advance()` branches on the glyph id read from the swapped shaped buffer, but for the pseudo-glyph preserved by the end-of-text insertion path that codepoint is uninitialized.
sink.note: The staged reproduction report and sanitizer trace both name `src/hb-ot-hmtx-table.hh:254:11` as the crash location for `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value`.

root_cause.description: The current-insertion path treats `!before` as sufficient to copy a current glyph, but on the witnessed end-of-text dispatch path there is no current glyph. The vulnerable source omits the required `buffer->idx < buffer->len` guard before `copy_glyph()` and `skip_glyph()`.
root_cause.note: For the statically parsed witness entry `flags = 0x004d`, `CurrentInsertBefore` and `DontAdvance` are both clear and `CurrentInsertCount = 2`. The fixing commit changes both sites to `if (buffer->idx < buffer->len && !before)`, explicitly handling end-of-text in the marked-insert and current-insert blocks.

parser_admitted.condition: The staged crash stack and reproduction report both belong to this first `hb_shape()` call on the fixed UTF-8 string `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`; the later UTF-32 branch at line 30 is not on the witnessed crashing path.

direct_publish.code: if (buffer->idx == buffer->len) break; ... for (; buffer->idx < buffer->len;) buffer->next_glyph (); buffer->swap_buffers ();
direct_publish.condition: Static PoC inspection shows the selected end-of-text entry encodes `CurrentInsertCount = 2` and clears `DontAdvance`, so line 668 issues `move_to(end + 2)`. That restores `idx == len`, makes the line-603 drain loop execute zero iterations, and sends the already-built output prefix directly to `swap_buffers()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSan reports the uninitialized value as created by this heap allocation while growing the fixed-text buffer's glyph-info array. The allocation gives the buffer spare capacity, but only the live entries written by later `hb_buffer_t::add()` calls are initialized; the logical one-past-end slot `info[len]` remains indeterminate when the end-of-text insertion bug copies it.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The first fixed-text `hb_buffer_add_utf8()` call in the harness triggers `ensure()` and `enlarge()` before the crashing `hb_shape()` invocation.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness builds the fixed UTF-8 buffer and shapes it with the attacker-controlled font; the reproduced crash is in this first `hb_shape()` call, not in the later UTF-32 branch.

The selected end-of-text insertion entry has `flags = 0x004d`, so the current-insert arm copies `info[len]`, executes two `output_glyph()` insertions, and advances the cursor past a nonexistent current glyph.

Because the same entry clears `DontAdvance`, `move_to(end + 2)` rewinds only the last inserted glyph; the copied pseudo-glyph stays inside the output prefix that `swap_buffers()` publishes as the shaped buffer.
Default positioning later reads the published pseudo-glyph's codepoint and `get_advance()` reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at the `glyph >= num_metrics` comparison.

fine_trace.note: MSan allocation origin. Growing the fixed-text buffer's `info` array creates heap capacity whose unused tail is not initialized by `realloc()`. The sanitizer origin stack traces the later poisoned value back to this allocation through `hb_buffer_add_utf<hb_utf8_t>` and `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` line 18.

Each real glyph appended to the fixed-text buffer zero-initializes only the active `info[len]` slot before filling its fields. Slots beyond the final logical glyph range remain whatever step 1's allocation left there, so `info[len]` is still indeterminate when shaping later reaches end-of-text.

After earlier loop iterations consume the real glyphs, `buffer->idx == buffer->len`, so the ternary at lines 558-560 selects `CLASS_END_OF_TEXT` and line 561 fetches the corresponding state-table entry from the attacker-controlled `morx` table. Static PoC inspection shows that the relevant insertion subtable at offset `0xad8` maps class 0 to entry 0, whose flags are `0x004d`.

fine_trace.var: count, start, glyphs, before, end, mark_set
fine_trace.note: The fetched end-of-text entry enables current insertion with `count = 2`, `start = 0`, `before = false`, and `end = buffer->out_len`. The same `flags = 0x004d` value clears `DontAdvance` and `SetMark`; because `driver_context_t` starts with `mark_set = false` and neither reachable entry in this subtable sets it, the marked-insert block is inactive and only the current-insert block executes on the crash path.

Root cause. The guard checks only `!before`, so on the end-of-text path it still executes `copy_glyph()` even though `buffer->idx == buffer->len` means there is no current glyph to copy. The fix adds `buffer->idx < buffer->len` to this condition and to the matching `skip_glyph()` guard.

With `idx == len`, `copy_glyph()` reads the logically one-past-end slot `info[len]` and copies that entire `hb_glyph_info_t` record into the output buffer at the saved position `out_info[end]`. Because steps 1-2 left that slot uninitialized, the copied pseudo-glyph carries an uninitialized `codepoint` and other fields. The MSan trace names this exact store as the point where the poisoned value was written to memory.

fine_trace.code: for (unsigned int i = 0; i < count; i++) buffer->output_glyph (glyphs[i]);
fine_trace.note: The current-insert loop executes exactly twice for `glyphs[0]` and `glyphs[1]`. `output_glyph()` copies `info[idx]` again without advancing `idx`, then overwrites only the inserted glyphs' `codepoint` fields, so the original pseudo-glyph at `out_info[end]` remains unchanged while `out_len` grows from `end + 1` to `end + 3`. The saved MSan origin frame at line 651 is the runtime evidence that this loop body executed on the witness.
Because `before` is still false, `skip_glyph()` runs even at end-of-text and advances `idx` from `len` to `len + 1`, creating the cursor state consumed by the later `move_to()` rewind.
The witness entry clears `DontAdvance`, so line 668 resolves to `move_to(end + count)`, i.e. `move_to(end + 2)`, not `move_to(end)`.

At entry to `move_to`, `out_len = end + 3`, `idx = len + 1`, and step 9 supplied `i = end + 2`, so the local rewind count is 1. `move_to()` therefore decrements `idx` back to `len` and `out_len` to `end + 2`, copying only the last inserted glyph back to `info[len]`. The copied pseudo-glyph at `out_info[end]` stays inside the live output prefix `[0, end + 2)`, which is the span later swapped into place.

fine_trace.code:
if (out_info != info) { info = out_info; out_info = tmp_string; }
len = out_len;
fine_trace.note: After step 10, `idx == len`, so the line-603 drain loop in `StateTableDriver::drive` copies no further glyphs before `swap_buffers()` runs. Swapping makes the output prefix of length `end + 2` the active `buffer->info` array; that live prefix still contains the copied pseudo-glyph at slot `end`.

During default positioning, HarfBuzz walks the swapped glyph buffer and reads each `info[i].codepoint` through `first_glyph`. When the loop reaches the preserved pseudo-glyph at slot `end`, `*first_glyph` is that uninitialized codepoint and is forwarded unchanged into `hmtx.get_advance()`.

MSan sink. The `glyph` parameter is the same scalar forwarded at step 12 from the copied pseudo-glyph's `codepoint`, so this comparison is the first executed use of the uninitialized value on the witnessed crash path.

allocation_context.note: The uninitialized value was created by a heap allocation in the `info` buffer growth path. The later bug is not a bad allocation size; it is the end-of-text insertion logic reading `info[len]` before that slot was ever initialized.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context only explains why `info[len]` is uninitialized; the actual bug is the missing end-of-text guard before `copy_glyph()`, followed by the same entry's executed `output_glyph()` loop and `move_to(end + 2)` preserving the copied slot until `swap_buffers()`.

format.name: OpenType/AAT font blob
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact 3608-byte font blob in `poc`, accepted by `hb_face_create()` and used by `hb-shape-fuzzer`. Static inspection of its `morx` table shows the insertion subtable at offset `0xad8` has an end-of-text entry 0 with `flags = 0x004d`, `currentInsertIndex = 0`, `markedInsertIndex = 0`, `CurrentInsertCount = 2`, `CurrentInsertBefore` clear, `DontAdvance` clear, and `SetMark` clear. During the first `hb_shape(font, buffer, NULL, 0)` call on the fixed UTF-8 text `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`, HarfBuzz reaches that entry with `mark_set` still false, so only the current-insertion branch runs: `copy_glyph()` reads `info[len]`, the loop executes `output_glyph()` twice for `insertionAction[0..1]`, `skip_glyph()` sets `idx = len + 1`, and `move_to(end + 2)` leaves the copied pseudo-glyph in the output prefix that `swap_buffers()` later publishes. The staged evidence does not justify a broader trigger class than fonts reproducing this exact end-of-text entry and preserving transition.
